text:
caroline: Heads-up — we are opening a limited preview for BYO TLS CA support on Private (VPC / on-prem). This lets customers supply their own CA bundle for TLS termination on the private control plane and agent endpoints. Goal is: customers who need stricter cert chains or internal PKIs can avoid our default certs. Sign-up form + docs below.

sam: Nice! timeline?

caroline: Preview starts next week (signup clsd beta) — invite-only for initial customers. Preview window: 6 weeks. GA target: mid-Q3, contingent on feedback and security review.

jess: What does "supply their own CA bundle" mean in practice? Is it just uploading a PEM or do we integrate with trust stores / ACME?

caroline: Initial preview = upload PEM for control plane TLS and agent-to-control-plane mTLS roots. We will not integrate ACME in preview. Longer term we may add PKCS#12, HSM-backed keys, and ACME automation.

ben: Any infra changes for customers? Ports, cert rotation, or required firewall rules?

infra: Customers need to allow outbound TLS from agents to the control plane and open the same ports we already document for Private. New piece: if you use a private CA that isn't globally trusted, you must provide the CA bundle to every agent host and to any internal tooling that talks to the control plane. We'll add a migration checklist.

caroline: Docs link: https://redwood.internal/docs/onprem/byo-tls-ca-preview (internal) — includes sample configuration, migration checklist, and security considerations. Also sign-up form: https://redwood.internal/forms/byo-tls-preview-signup

jess: Sample config?

caroline: Example snippet for agent config (preview):

```
agent: 
  endpoint: https://controlplane.redwood.example.edu:443
  tls: 
    ca_bundle_path: /etc/redwood/ca-bundle.pem
    require_client_mtls: true
```

caroline: The control-plane will accept PEM bundles signed by the provided CA and will validate client cert chains against the uploaded root(s). Rotation: customers can upload a new bundle; agents will pick up the new bundle on next restart or via config reload API (we'll provide both).

security-bot: Security note: preview will be gated by a lightweight security assessment. Customers must attest that keys are generated and stored per our minimal best practices. No private keys should be uploaded to our control plane. Only roots/CA bundles are allowed.

legal-team: Action for commercial teams: include the BYO CA addendum in pilot contracts. We need to ensure indemnities around customer-supplied trust roots. Legal will post the addendum template to the pilot workspace.

ben: Any telemetry impact? Are we collecting cert fingerprints or metadata?

caroline: We will collect only SHA256 fingerprint of the uploaded CA bundle for operational tracking and order lookup. No plaintext keys, no cert contents beyond bundle fingerprints and size/subject summary. Customers can opt-out of telemetry via the existing telemetry toggles.

docs: We'll add migration steps, troubleshooting, and a FAQ. Expect a first-draft doc in the repo by EOD Friday. Please flag any required diagrams or flowcharts.

sam: Are there known limitations for the preview (e.g., cross-region, multi-CA chains)?

caroline: Limitations in preview:
- Multi-root chains supported but customers are responsible for ordering.
- No ACME or automated public cert issuance.
- Some integrations (monitoring agents from partners) may require manual config to trust the CA.
- Rollbacks: if a bad bundle is uploaded, we support restoring the previous bundle via the UI or API — follow the rollback playbook.

ops-bot: Reminder: Onboarding slots are limited. Signup form closes when we hit capacity.

jess: For customers currently using our default certs, what will change at GA?

caroline: Default behavior won't change. BYO CA is opt-in. At GA, API will be stable, and we'll add P12 support + KMS/HSM integration for customer-hosted key material (not in preview).

security-bot: Please ensure any pilot customers complete the short security checklist before enabling BYO. Security will run a remote attestation call for at least the first 5 customers.

ben: Do we need product analytics events?

caroline: Minimal events: preview_opt_in, ca_bundle_uploaded, ca_bundle_rotated. No cert contents. Product should track totals and pilot churn.

caroline: Call to action: If you're on eng/infra/docs/legal/security/ops and need to be part of the preview-ready workstream, DM me. Customer-facing pilot invites will go out Monday. If you manage pilot sales/AE, PM me the customer list before EOD Friday.

sam: Thanks — will coordinate with infra for rollout scripts.

jess: I'll review the docs draft and add a troubleshooting section.

caroline: Thanks all :party:
